name: Appendix: Tomb of the Shadow Serpents

entries: An Adventure For {@b Level 1} Characters
This adventure is designed to fill one or two sessions of play. It can take place in any region where there are forests and caves.

entries.name: Key Plot Points
entries: The following information is key to this adventure's story:

items.name: Venger's Schemes
items.entry: The characters receive a mysterious missive from {@creature Venger|AU} (see {@area chapter 6|32a|x}), a fiendish mage who invites them to plumb the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents in search of treasure. In reality, {@creature Venger|AU} wishes to test whether the characters would be useful tools for his schemes.

items.name: Escape the Tomb
items.entry: The characters venture into the tomb and discover many fallen heroes who previously tried to claim {@creature Venger|AU|Venger's} treasure. If the characters survive, they can keep the magic items they find, and they pique Venger's interest. If they die, their bones will lie in the tomb forever.

entries.name: Preparation

images.title: Map 7.1 Tomb of the Shadow Serpents

entries: Before running the adventure, prepare as follows:

items.name: Step 1
items.entry: Read the "Adventure Background" section. Optionally, read the description of the {@book Shadowfell|XDMG|5|Shadowfell} in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|5|Shadowfell} or on D&D Beyond.

items.name: Step 2
items.entry: Review area {@area T12|368|x} and familiarize yourself with the Shadowfell Despair table in the {@table Shadowfell Despair|XDMG|Dungeon Master's Guide} description of the Shadowfell. If you find it too complicated to use the table's effects in area T12, feel free to skip them.

items.name: Step 3
items.entry: Make a copy of the {@book Serpent Puzzle Piece handouts|AU|7|Handout: Serpent Puzzle Piece 1}. (You will share these with the other players at certain points during the adventure.)

items.name: Step 4
items.entry: Bookmark the following stat blocks in the {@book Monster Manual|XMM} or on D&D Beyond:

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: The fiendish, immortal mage {@creature Venger|AU} weaves interlocking schemes across the D&D multiverse to amass power and thwart his enemies. Some of Venger's schemes involve allying with—or opposing—heroes he manipulates to his own ends.

To identify heroes who might prove useful in future plots, {@creature Venger|AU} has built tombs across the multiverse as testing grounds. When heroes' deeds catch his attention, he invites those heroes to claim the treasure inside the tombs. {@creature Venger|AU} often challenges heroes to explore numerous tombs before he's convinced of their usefulness.

The offer of treasure is real—though {@creature Venger|AU} considers the treasures in his tombs inconsequential, adventurers might find them worth the risk. But the tombs are deadly, and they've become the final resting place for many adventurers who've failed Venger's challenges.

Among the earliest tombs {@creature Venger|AU} built is the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents. It's situated within a cave on the Material Plane near an intersection with the Shadowfell, so strange and gloomy environs envelop the tomb. The tomb holds deadly monsters and traps. Surviving the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents is the first step toward earning Venger's respect.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: For this adventure, your characters need to know only that a powerful individual has challenged them to explore the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents in search of treasure. You might make it clear that {@creature Venger|AU} has invited them, or you could obscure his identity, allowing the characters to deduce the tomb's creator while they explore or even once they've completed the adventure.
If you want to further entice the characters, use one of the following adventure hooks to draw them into the story:

items.name: A Deadly Rivalry
items.entry: The characters are embroiled in competition with another group and wish to prove their superior skills. Perhaps the characters are working for one of the magical factions described in {@area chapter 4|1c1|x} and wish to claim the tomb's treasure before another faction does. Or perhaps the characters have caught wind that rivals who compete with them for quests are also headed toward the tomb, and the characters hope to claim its treasure first. Regardless of the details, the characters can claim treasure—and bragging rights—if they survive the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents.

items.name: Impress a Patron
items.entry: The characters are cultivating a relationship with a powerful patron who might fund their continued adventures. Perhaps the characters want to impress a potential patron—such as one of the group patrons described in {@area chapter 3|170|x}—or they're trying to cement a fledgling relationship with a patron. Either way, the patron loves magical lore and tales of adventure. Emerging victorious from the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents is sure to get the patron's attention and prove the characters' capabilities.

entries: There was once good in Venger's heart. I believe it might return once more, but until then, be wary. He has proven a true fiend.

entries.name: Beginning the Adventure
entries: The characters receive a message from {@creature Venger|AU}. This might reach the characters in a nonmagical way, such as a letter delivered by a messenger, or it might reach them via magic such as a {@spell Magic Mouth|XPHB} or {@spell Programmed Illusion|XPHB} spell.

For players excited to play an adventure involving {@creature Venger|AU}, consider beginning with a {@i Programmed Illusion} spell (spell save {@dc 19}) that activates when the characters reach the forest in which the tomb is located. When the illusion activates, the characters see a winged, one-horned fiend astride a flying black horse. The fiend swoops down from above and delivers the message in a deep, booming voice before flying away again.
If the journey to the tomb is more than a short distance away, include directions in this message as necessary:

"Would-be heroes! Should you desire fame and treasure, heed this challenge. My Tomb of the Shadow Serpents lies nearby, built within a cave of unrelieved gloom. Seek out the stone doors that bear a serpent; within lies what you seek."

"I eagerly await heroes worthy of claiming the tomb's riches. Many die terrible deaths within, but perhaps you shall be different. Test your mettle in my tomb, and perhaps one day we shall meet again to our mutual benefit."
If Venger's message is delivered in writing, it is signed with a capital {@i V}.

entries.name: Reaching the Tomb
entries: Summarize the trip to the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents with this description:

The journey to the tomb is short and uneventful. As you venture further into the forest, the foliage becomes denser, and signs of folk living nearby or even passing through become scant. Soon, a hillock rises before you, and in its side yawns a gloomy cave maw. This must be the cave mentioned in the message!
The cave opening is area {@area T1|33f|x}, which is described below.

entries.name: Tomb of the Shadow Serpents
entries: The Tomb of the Shadow Serpents has served {@creature Venger|AU} for generations as a testing ground for adventurers. Before inviting adventurers to brave it, {@creature Venger|AU} resets or repairs the tomb's features and replenishes its treasure to ensure there are always challenges and rewards for heroes who survive it. He never gives another thought to those who die here, leaving their bodies to litter the tomb.

entries.name: Tomb Features
entries: The Tomb of the Shadow Serpents consists of a mix of rooms with carved stone walls and natural cave chambers. Areas {@area T1|33f|x}, {@area T5|350|x}, {@area T8|35c|x}, {@area T9|361|x}, and {@area T10|363|x} are cave chambers, while areas {@area T2|342|x}, {@area T3|346|x}, {@area T4|34c|x}, {@area T6|354|x}, {@area T7|359|x}, {@area T11|365|x}, and {@area T12|368|x} are constructed from stone.
The tomb has the following additional features.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: The ceilings of the tomb's cave chambers are 30 feet high. The ceilings of stone chambers are 20 feet high.

entries.name: Doors
entries: Doors are made of stone and unlocked, except for the door that leads to the sepulcher (area {@area T11|365|x}), which is locked with the serpent puzzle described in "{@area Serpent Puzzle|33c|x}."

entries.name: Fallen Adventurers
entries: Throughout the tomb are the bodies of adventurers who have fallen to the place's perils. These adventurers might be of any species appropriate for your setting—such as a mix of dwarves, humans, and orcs. Area descriptions include visual clues about how the adventurers died. Any character who notices a fallen adventurer can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the body and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check; on a successful check, they determine the adventurer succumbed to a nearby trap—or to a nearby monster, as in area T8.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: In the tomb's stone chambers and in its cave entrance, sconces shaped like shadowy serpents fill the area with {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}. The tomb's interior cave chambers are areas of {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}; descriptions of these areas assume characters have a way of seeing in the dark.

entries.name: Serpent Puzzle
entries: The mosaic on the double door in area {@area T11|365|x} that leads to the sepulcher is identical to the mosaic on the door in area {@area T1|33f|x}. The mosaic is shown below. Each mosaic depicts a stylized, shadowy serpent. The mosaic on the sepulcher door, however, is missing three obsidian pieces that combine to form the shape of the serpent. These puzzle pieces are scattered throughout the tomb.

Serpent puzzle pieces are located in areas {@area T6|354|x}, {@area T8|35c|x}, and {@area T10|363|x}, as shown on the map. Each puzzle piece is made from obsidian and worth 10 GP. A character who examines a piece realizes it's a broken part of an obsidian mosaic identical to the one in the door that leads into the tomb. The characters must place the puzzle pieces correctly back into the broken mosaic (or bypass the puzzle; see area {@area T11|365|x}) before they can enter the sepulcher.

entries.name: Walls
entries: The walls of cave chambers are made of earth and thick tree roots. The walls of stone chambers are made from slabs of solid stone.

entries.name: Tomb Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 1.

entries.name: T1: Cave Entrance
entries: When the characters are ready to venture into the cave described in "Reaching the Tomb," read or paraphrase the following:

Three hulking, wolflike beasts lumber around this wide cave entrance, their red, malevolent eyes peering at you. Gray light flickering from sconces reflects off an obsidian mosaic in a double door at the back of the cave entrance. The mosaic depicts an S-shaped serpent.
Three {@creature Worg|XMM|Worgs} lurk here and begin combat when the characters move 10 feet into the cave.

The worgs recently adopted the cave entrance as their home, assuming that creatures living inside the double door would periodically emerge and provide the worgs with scrumptious meals. The characters are the worgs' first potential victims, and the hungry creatures fight to the death. The worgs don't know about {@creature Venger|AU} or care about the purpose of the tomb.

entries.name: Serpent Mosaic
entries: The obsidian serpent mosaic on the double door is one foot wide and one foot tall. It's identical to the mosaic the characters must reconstruct to open the serpent puzzle door in area {@area T11|365|x}.

entries.name: T2: Tomb Entryway

entries: A stone double door stands in the east wall of this chamber, and another stands in the west wall. Flanking the path that leads deeper into the temple are two identical statues. Each is seven feet tall and depicts a one-horned, winged man wearing robes and an ominous grin.

These statues depict {@area Venger|32a|x}, as any character familiar with the mage easily recognizes. Any character unfamiliar with {@creature Venger|AU} can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a statue and make a {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Religion|XPHB}) check to try to identify the statue's likeness.

entries.name: Statue Traps
entries: The statues are magical traps. The first time a creature moves within 5 feet of a statue, that statue intones in a deep, commanding voice, "Clasp my hand for a boon."

If a creature touches a statue's hand, a fiery jolt of energy discharges and the creature makes a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw, taking 5 ({@dice 1d10}) Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. On a success or failure, the statue's magical voice chuckles and shouts, "Expect no favors!" Each statue activates only once.

entries.name: Detecting the Traps
entries: A {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} spell reveals an aura of Evocation magic around each statue. As a {@action Search|XPHB} action, a creature within 5 feet of a statue can examine it and make a {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check, noticing that the statue's hand emits warmth. The traps can't be disarmed, but they can be avoided by simply not touching the statues' hands.

entries.name: T3: Deadly Corridor

entries: A desiccated corpse wearing rusty armor lies sprawled on this corridor's floor. The circlet on the corpse's head is strangely pristine and glints in the sconces' light, and a serpent-shaped blade protrudes from the body. Double doors lead east, west, and south.
This T-shaped corridor leads deeper into the tomb.

entries.name: Blade Traps
entries: There are two pressure plates in this corridor, as denoted on the map. When a creature moves onto a pressure plate for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, a gap opens in the adjacent wall, and a serpent-shaped blade flies toward the creature. The creature on the plate must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take 3 ({@dice 1d6}) Slashing damage. Each trap activates once per turn. Once a trap has activated three times, the trap ceases to function.

entries.name: Detecting and Disarming the Traps
entries: As a {@action Search|XPHB} action, a creature can examine a section of floor that forms a pressure plate and make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check, detecting the pressure plate on a successful check. Wedging an {@item Iron Spikes|XPHB|Iron Spike} or similar object under the pressure plate prevents the trap from triggering.

entries.name: Fallen Adventurer
entries: Except for the circlet, the fallen adventurer's equipment is dented and unusable.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The circlet on the corpse's head is a {@item Circlet of Blasting|XDMG}.

entries.name: T4: Mud Pit

entries: Spanning most of this chamber is a large pit of bubbling mud, from which rise shimmering waves of heat. A rickety bridge made of chains and decaying wooden planks crosses the pit.

The chain bridge is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. When a creature steps on the bridge for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw or fall into the mud pit. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

entries.name: Mud Pit
entries: The area of the mud pit acts like a 10-foot-deep quicksand pit hazard (see the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}), but the mud is also dangerously hot thanks to a natural underground hot spring. Any creature that starts its turn in the mud takes 3 ({@dice 1d6}) Fire damage.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The western alcove is full of detritus covered in dried mud. A thorough search of the alcove takes 1 minute and yields a {@item Potion of Fire Breath|XDMG}.

entries.name: T5: Spiderling Den

entries: The air in this dark, enormous cave is cool and damp. Thick spiderwebs cover the center of the floor and the entrance to a tunnel leading away to the east. A lumpy, five-foot-wide sac of webbing bulges from the eastern wall next to the tunnel's entrance.

Six juvenile giant spiders (use the {@creature Giant Wolf Spider|XMM} stat block) lurk within the webs in the center of this chamber. They're the young of the giant spiders in area T10. A character who takes a {@action Search|XPHB} action to survey the webs and succeeds on a {@dc 17} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check notices the spiders.
As soon as a character ventures within 10 feet of the webs, the spiders emerge and begin combat. They fight to the death.

entries.name: Webs
entries: Areas covered in webs, as denoted on the map, use the rules for the webs hazard (see {@hazard Webs|XDMG}).

entries.name: Egg Sac
entries: The sac on the eastern wall holds unhatched spider eggs. The sac has AC 10; HP 8; {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Fire damage; and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Piercing, Poison, and Psychic damage. The sac is unaffected if the webs around it are destroyed.
Ten minutes after a character first enters this area, the eggs hatch and four {@creature Spider|XMM|Spiders} emerge. The spiders fight the characters on sight.

entries.name: T6: Long Corridor

entries: On this corridor's floor slump three corpses with darts protruding from their flesh. The center body clutches a shiny, black object in one hand.
Bloodstains splatter the floor of this hallway.

entries.name: Dart Traps
entries: There are three pressure plates in this corridor, as denoted on {@area the map|07b|x}. Each pressure plate triggers a poisoned darts trap (see the {@trap Poisoned Darts|XDMG|Dungeon Master's Guide}).

entries.name: Fallen Adventurers
entries: The adventurers' equipment is dented and unusable.

entries.name: Serpent Puzzle Piece
entries: The body in the center of the corridor clutches a piece of the serpent mosaic in area {@area T11|365|x}. When the characters find this piece, show them the {@book Serpent Puzzle Piece 1 handout|AU|7|Handout: Serpent Puzzle Piece 1}.

entries.name: T7: Hall of Armor

entries: Resting on a dais at the west end of this chamber are two suits of shining plate armor. Each suit is arranged on a stand whose wooden base is adorned with silver filigree. A few stairs lead up to the dais.
Both suits are {@creature Animated Armor|XMM}. As soon as a character ventures within 5 feet of the stairs, the suits begin combat.

When a character is within 5 feet of an animated armor, they notice a seal etched on the armor's chest that depicts the ominously grinning face of a one-horned fiend—identical to the faces of the statues of {@creature Venger|AU} in area {@area T2|342|x}.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The wooden base of each armor stand includes a small drawer. The drawers are locked. As a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, a character can try to pick the lock using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, doing so with a successful {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check.
The drawer in the south stand holds two obsidian stones worth 10 GP each. The drawer in the north stand holds a {@item Bag of Tricks|XDMG} (tan).

entries.name: T8: Lacedons' Lair

entries: This wide cavern's walls are slick with trickling water that forms a murky, ten-foot-wide pool. To the east of the pool lies a one-armed corpse, next to which glints a shiny, black object. Strange gurgles emanate from the cavern's western end.

Two {@creature Lacedon Ghoul|XMM|Lacedon Ghouls} lurk in this cavern. One is around a corner in the western alcove, chewing on an arm it severed from the body in the northeast corner. Another is underwater in the pool, waiting to ambush trespassers.

As soon as a character ventures within 5 feet of the fallen adventurer or comes within 25 feet of the western wall, the underwater ghoul jumps out of the pool and fights them. The sounds of combat beginning alert the ghoul in the western alcove; that ghoul drops the arm it's chewing on and joins the fight.

entries.name: Fallen Adventurer
entries: The ghouls killed an adventurer and have been snacking on the corpse, which is covered in bite marks. The adventurer's equipment is dented and unusable.

entries.name: Murky Pool
entries: The pool is 5 feet deep and filled with cool, mineral-laden water.

entries.name: Serpent Puzzle Piece
entries: Next to the body is a piece of the serpent mosaic in area T11. When the characters find this piece, show them the {@book Serpent Puzzle Piece 2 handout|AU|7|Handout: Serpent Puzzle Piece 2}.

entries.name: T9: Webbed Tunnel

entries.title: Enormous, hairy spiders lurk in the tomb's depths, waiting to feed on unprepared adventurers.

entries: Thick spiderwebs cover the floor, walls, and ceiling of this tunnel.
The area of this tunnel is a webs hazard (see the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|2|Hazards}).

entries.name: T10: Spiders' Nest

entries: Thick webs spill from this long cave's western opening. Perched on gossamer mounds of webbing to the north and south are two enormous spiders with hairy legs. On the northeast wall, a severed hand suspended in the webs holds a shiny, black object.
There are two {@creature Giant Spider|XMM|Giant Spiders} here: one in the northeast corner and one in the southeast alcove. As soon as the characters enter this cave, the spiders fight them.
The spiders are hungry and fight to the death. They long ago ate the body the severed hand came from.

entries.name: Serpent Puzzle Piece
entries: The severed hand holds a piece of the serpent mosaic in area T11. When the characters find this piece, show them the {@book Serpent Puzzle Piece 3 handout|AU|7|Handout: Serpent Puzzle Piece 3}.

entries.name: T11: Serpent Puzzle Door

entries: The stone double door at the west end of this hall bears a mosaic similar to the one outside the tomb. But the space that held an obsidian, S-shaped serpent in the entrance's mosaic is empty in this one. Softly glowing blue lines illuminate the serpent-shaped void.
This door's magical lock is linked to the mosaic. The glowing lines in the mosaic's empty spaces thrum with magic.

entries.name: Serpent Mosaic
entries: The mosaic is one foot wide and one foot tall. Placing the three missing pieces of the mosaic's obsidian serpent in the mosaic unlocks the door. The pieces are located in the long corridor (area {@area T6|354|x}), the lacedons' lair (area {@area T8|35c|x}), and the spiders' nest (area {@area T10|363|x}).

Alternatively, a character can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to trace the glowing lines and simulate the puzzle pieces' correct placement. A character who does so makes a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check. On a successful check, the door unlocks.

entries.name: T12: The Shadowy Sepulcher

entries.title: The shadows that haunt the sepulcher were once heroes who betrayed {@creature Venger|AU}.

entries: Before you stands an eight-foot-tall central statue, around which swirl tendrils of wispy, black shadow. The statue is made of faceted obsidian and depicts entwined serpents whose heads rise toward the ceiling. On a dais to the west are three sarcophagi, their marble lids carved with the likenesses of warriors in repose.
Three {@creature Shadow|XMM|Shadows} lurk in this room, each hidden in one of the sarcophagi. As soon as a character ventures west of the serpent statue, the shadows emerge and begin combat.

The shadows arose from the bodies of adventurers {@creature Venger|AU} killed for betraying him. The mage then bound the shadows to this room. In a cruel act of irony, {@creature Venger|AU} built elaborate sarcophagi for the adventurers' bodies and placed them here, taunting the shadows with the prospect of eternal rest.

entries.name: Serpent Statue
entries: {@creature Venger|AU} built the serpent statue and imbued it with magic he drew from the Shadowfell. As a result, the statue causes this room to behave as if the room were on that plane. It also causes the shadows to take on a serpentine appearance.

A character who enters this room must succeed on a {@dc 10} Wisdom saving throw or be affected by despair. Roll on the Shadowfell Despair table in the {@table Shadowfell Despair|XDMG|Dungeon Master's Guide} to determine the form the despair takes.

The statue has AC 15, HP 18, and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Radiant damage. If the statue is reduced to 0 HP, the Shadowfell stops affecting this room, and any despair effects on the characters end immediately.

A character who takes the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the statue and succeeds on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check understands how the statue is affecting the room and surmises that its connection to the Shadowfell gives it {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Radiant damage.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The sarcophagus lids are made of solid marble. A character can take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to make a {@dc 12} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check, lifting one of the lids on a successful check.

Inside each sarcophagus are the desiccated remains of an adventurer, whose equipment is rusted and unusable. The north sarcophagus also holds a bloodstone worth 50 GP. The central sarcophagus holds a {@item Cube of Summoning|XDMG}. The south sarcophagus holds three turquoises worth 10 GP apiece.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: Once the characters are finished exploring the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents, award each character 100 XP for completing the adventure. The characters should have enough XP to advance to level 2 by the end of the adventure. If you're using a method of level advancement that doesn't rely on XP, the characters gain a level after defeating the shadows in the sepulcher.

If the characters survive the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents, {@creature Venger|AU} notices their prowess. He tracks the characters throughout their adventuring careers and might challenge them to explore other tombs he's created throughout the multiverse.

Dungeons in several published D&D adventures can be easily repurposed as tombs that {@creature Venger|AU} challenges the characters to explore. The temple in the level 4 adventure "The Will of Orcus" in {@adventure Dragon Delves|DrDe-TWoO|1}, for example, could be reimagined as such a tomb, with the cultists of the demon lord Orcus instead becoming sycophantic followers of {@creature Venger|AU}. The Tomb of the Nine Gods in {@adventure Tomb of Annihilation|ToA|7}, meant for level 9 adventurers, could similarly be reimagined as a complex created by {@creature Venger|AU} instead of the lich Acererak. The Tomb of Wayward Souls in {@adventure Vecna: Eve of Ruin|VEoR|7}, another dungeon created by Acererak, is appropriate for level 16 characters. You can also create new tombs that {@creature Venger|AU} challenges the characters to explore.

At your discretion, after the characters have survived the dangers of numerous tombs, {@creature Venger|AU} might offer the characters mysterious jobs such as finding an item, stopping or delivering a shipment of goods, or protecting a public figure. These schemes should feed into Venger's attempts to thwart the League of Malevolence, an odious assemblage of power-hungry villains led by Venger's former lackey, the human mage Kelek. The characters shouldn't trust {@creature Venger|AU}, but they might accept his jobs (which always pay well) out of curiosity or as part of a plan to double-cross him.
